notes.1ai: Most candidates read the force meters correctly and calculated the weight of the ruler.
notes.1aii: Only stronger candidates gave suitable procedures. Candidates that drew a diagram were more likely to answer this correctly .
notes.1b: Most candidates correctly recorded their values to a consistent number of decimal p laces . A few had decreasing values indicating that they had used the ruler the wrong way round.
notes.1c: Most candidates understood how to sketch a graph, labelling the axes correctly, with the appropriate quantity and units. Most candidates correctly plotted their points accurately . A few candidates used blobs that were too large. There were many good thin lines plotted. Lines of best fit should have an even distribution of points on either side and candidates should not assume the line will pass through the origin.
notes.1d: Most candidates correctly read their intercept and calculated the weight of the ruler.
notes.1e: Most candidates stated it was easy to choose the line of best fit but very few gave a valid justification.
notes.2ai: Almost all candidates correctly stated the room temperature with the correct units.
notes.2aii: Most candidates correctly described a technique for a correct reading.
notes.2b: Most candidates correctly recorded the temperature.
notes.2c: Most values were correctly calculated with the correct units and decreasing answers were seen.
notes.2di: Many candidates identified the pattern correctly but fewer made any relevant justification from their results.
notes.2dii: Most candidates realised that the temperature would have returned to, or be close to, room temperature.
notes.2ei: Many candidates identified that the cooling rate would be lower but very few gave a valid explanation.
notes.2eii: Most candidates gained credit here with the volume of water or room temperature being the most commonly seen answers .
notes.3ai: Most candidates correctly read the meters and had decreasing values for current.
notes.3aii: Most candidates correctly calculated the values of resistance .
notes.3b: (c) Most candidates correctly recorded increasing values of resistance, but not all responses were consistent to 2 or 3 significant figures.
notes.3di: Most calculations were correct but not all were within 10 per cent of each other.
notes.3dii: Many candidates made a correct statement but not all gave an appropriate justification.
notes.3e: Few candidates realised that the purpose was to limit the current from becoming too large .
notes.3f: There were many vague answers seen which did not fully answer the question.
